input: How do you start Redis for a Kubernetes work queue?
expected_output: Apply redis-pod.yaml and redis-service.yaml using kubectl apply -f with the URLs https://k8s.io/examples/application/job/redis/redis-pod.yaml and https://k8s.io/examples/application/job/redis/redis-service.yaml.
gold_context:
For this example, you will start a single instance of Redis.

Run the following commands:

    kubectl apply -f https://k8s.io/examples/application/job/redis/redis-pod.yaml
    kubectl apply -f https://k8s.io/examples/application/job/redis/redis-service.yaml

input: How do you connect to Redis and add a task to the job2 work queue?
expected_output: Connect with redis-cli -h redis, then use rpush job2 followed by a task value, for example rpush job2 "apple".
gold_context:
Once the prompt appears, connect to Redis and fill the queue (named "job2"):

    redis-cli -h redis

    # Inside the redis prompt:
    rpush job2 "apple"
    rpush job2 "banana"
    rpush job2 "cherry"

input: Does each pod process only one item in the documented Kubernetes work queue example?
expected_output: No. Each pod picks up an item, processes it, and repeats until the end of the queue is reached.
gold_context:
In this example, as each pod is created, it picks up one unit of work
from a task queue, processes it, and repeats until the end of the queue is reached.

input: Which kubectl commands confirm that the Metrics Server is collecting data?
expected_output: Run kubectl top nodes and kubectl top pods --all-namespaces. They should show CPU and memory usage for nodes and pods.
gold_context:
$ kubectl top nodes
$ kubectl top pods --all-namespaces
If the Metrics Server is properly installed and functioning, you should see CPU and memory usage metrics for nodes and pods in your cluster.

input: Why is the Metrics Server needed before testing Kubernetes autoscaling?
expected_output: It collects node and pod resource usage metrics needed for autoscaling decisions.
gold_context: The Metrics Server collects resource usage metrics from the cluster’s nodes and pods, which are necessary for autoscaling decisions.
